beats.say: This is the switch inside electric cars, laptops and almost every power supply.
A MOSFET has a gate, a drain and a source. A voltage on the gate switches it on.
A normal transistor needs a base current. A MOSFET's gate draws almost no current at all.
Fully on, its resistance can be tiny, so it barely heats up, even switching big currents.
Next time: the relay. Subscribe so you don't miss it.
